summary: Several comments treat all entries in `System.getProperties()` as map-visible, but the implementation exposes only string-keyed, string-valued entries.

items.issue: The iterator is described as covering currently set System properties and omitting `null` values, but it obtains keys through `stringPropertyNames()`. Properties with a non-`String` key or value are omitted even when set and non-null.
items.suggestion: Describe it as iterating over string-valued System properties, and retain the access-denied behavior.

items.issue: It can return `true` when System properties exist but none have string keys and string values, because it delegates to `iterator`. The documentation says this means no System property is set.
items.suggestion: Qualify the result as referring to the string-valued properties exposed by this map.

items.issue: `stringPropertyNames()` omits entries whose key or value is not a `String`; the comment instead promises names of all currently set System properties.
items.suggestion: State that it returns names of the string-valued System properties exposed by this map.

items.issue: A property with a non-`String` value is present in the Java `Properties` object but `System.getProperty` returns `null`, so this method returns `None`. The documentation says `None` only means unset or unreadable.
items.suggestion: Include the non-string-value case in the `@return` description, or describe lookup in terms of string-valued properties.

items.issue: Via the map lookup, this is false for an existing property whose value is not a `String`, yet the comment says it reports whether a System property is set.
items.suggestion: Say that it tests whether a string-valued System property with that name is set.
